HD.rationale: HD is a structurally dominant franchise (52% U.S. home improvement share, Pro ecosystem, expanding TAM to $1.2T) but is in a clear period of fundamental softening with no near-term catalyst for reversal. EPS declined -1.4% YoY on the latest filing (Q3 FY2025), OCF contracted -5.3% YoY, and operating margin compressed from 13.5% to 13.1%. The Q4 FY2025 picture is worse: operating margin fell to ~10%, ROIC dropped from 31.3% to 25.7%, and FCF declined from $3.1B to $2.3B. The balance sheet carries $65B in total debt with liabilities/equity at 7.8x. Valuation at 23.2x P/E offers essentially zero equity-risk premium versus the 10-year yield of 4.34%, and ROE has halved from 2.53x to 1.20x while the P/E has barely moved — the market is not re-pricing the earnings deterioration. The macro overlay is hostile: WTI crude has surged +64% in 90 days to $99.27/bbl, a direct and unreflected margin headwind for a retailer with large freight/distribution costs. Management itself guides comps flat to +2% for FY2026, with CEO Decker stating 'we have not yet seen a catalyst for an inflection in housing activity' and turnover at 30-to-40-year lows with no recovery expected through 2027. Q1 FY2026 consensus EPS of $3.42 is -3.9% YoY. The acquisition strategy (SRS, GMS, Mingledorff's) is diluting margins and leveraging the balance sheet precisely when organic demand is softest. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating fundamentals, no valuation margin of safety, and no credible near-term re-rating catalyst.
